.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 1234 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026

 - Hazardous beach conditions through Tuesday evening and again
   Thursday through Saturday

 - Seasonal to slightly below seasonal temperatures through Thursday

 - Light rain for Tuesday except interior Central Coast

&&

.SHORT TERM...
Issued at 1229 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026
(Today and tonight)

The system that brought precip over the weekend is now carving its
way through the Four Corners region. In its wake upper level
ridging is currently building over the CA. As such, expect warmer
and drier conditions to kick off the work week. Speaking of the
weekend rain, residual low level moisture may lead to some patchy
fog, but widespread fog impacts are looking less likely this
morning. High clouds associated with the next rain maker are
spilling over the ridge, which is limiting radiational cooling
potential. Temperatures this afternoon will be a few degrees 
warmer than Sunday and in the 60s to lower 70s. 

The dry weather will be short-lived as the next rain maker will
make is presence known after midnight tonight. The ridge weakens
and moves eastward. Behind the ridge is another upper level low.
This feature will bring precip back to the region. Rain chances
initially develop over the North Bay late tonight.

&&

.LONG TERM...
Issued at 1229 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026
(Tuesday through Sunday)

Will likely be a wet commute Tuesday morning as the associated
surface low begins to move closer to the coast. Precip chances
will spread S and E through the day, but loose some steam over the
interior Central Coast. In addition to precip, instability
increase over the northern coastal waters during the afternoon. 
Thunderstorms have been added to the forecast. Will leave them out
of the forecast over land at this time, but some hi-res models suggest
instability does briefly drift into Sonoma county during the 
afternoon. Thunder may need to be added on the next forecast 
update. Precip chances linger into early Tuesday before drier 
weather returns by Wednesday. Rainfall amounts will be greatest 
over the North Bay 0.10-0.50", Bay Area 0.01-0.25", Central Coast 
little to no accum.

Wednesday kicks off a warming and drying trend that will last 
into next weekend with quasi-zonal flow transitioning to ridging 
aloft. Temperature rebound will be impressive too as highs reach 
the 70s to lower 80s next weekend.

Looking out into fantasy land the Pacific stays active with
additional rain chance on the horizon. Next rain chance return
around Nov 10-11.  

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 319 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026

Currently VFR with high clouds streaming in from the west. Low 
confidence on fog development tonight with high clouds limiting
radiational cooling; however, STS was briefly IFR earlier. High 
confidence in VFR and diurnal winds prevailing through the TAF 
period. Towards the end of the 24 hour TAF period and into the 
next one, winds will increase and shift to become southerly ahead 
of the cold front. Rain showers will spread from northwest to 
southeast starting at 15Z tomorrow. Low probability for 
thunderstorms with the best chances farther north.

Vicinity of SFO...Currently VFR with westerly flow. High confidence 
in VFR through most of the TAF period. An approaching cold front 
will lower clouds through the TAF period and bring rain showers to 
the terminal as early as 15Z tomorrow. Brief reductions in ceiling
and visibility will be possible with rain showers, likely MVFR. 
Winds will be light and diurnal today before increasing and 
backing tonight to become southerly ahead of the cold front.

SFO Bridge Approach...Low clouds below FL070 will begin to filter
in as early as 07Z.

Monterey Bay Terminals...Currently VFR with easterly flow at MRY and 
VFR with drainage flow at SNS. High confidence in VFR and diurnal 
winds prevailing through the TAF period. 

&&

.MARINE...
(Today through Saturday)
Issued at 319 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026

Rough seas will build into the outer waters tonight through
Wednesday morning, bringing hazardous conditions for small craft.
Gentle to moderate northwesterly breezes will increase and back
tonight to become moderate to fresh southwesterly breezes ahead
of an approaching cold front. Rain with a low chance of
thunderstorms is expected Tuesday as a result with the greatest
chances north of Pigeon Point. Moderate to fresh northerly
breezes and moderate to rough seas will prevail Wednesday through
Friday.

&&

.BEACHES...
Issued at 1229 AM PST Mon Nov 2 2026

Hazardous beach conditions will be present at Pacific Coast beaches 
Monday and Tuesday as long period (15-19 second) northwesterly swell 
will bring an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip 
currents. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, 
pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. Stay 
off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside infrastructure. 
Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf and never turn your 
back on the ocean!
